A high concentration of non-white population does exist in various areas. Based on census information, some areas (census tracts) range up to 75 percent non-white, while others are as low as 0.1 percent in non-white population. Census tracts with the higher concentrations of non-whites appear to be strung across the geographic center of the City in a diagonal pattern running from northwest to southeast. The project area appears at the north westernmost end of the diagonal. Specific racial trends relating specifically to the project will be discussed later in this report.
j. Air pollution levels
Available data on air pollution sources in Harrisburg indicate that there are eleven industrial point sources of air pollution emission in the City. Information, largely for Harrisburg West, shows that air quality there is classified as "background" pollution to "heavily polluted". The criteria accompanying these classifications are levels of suspended particulate matter, sulfation rates (measure of SO<sub>2</sub>), and levels of settleable particulate matter.
k. Education
A number of public school districts cover the community area of the project. There is also a Catholic parochial school system headquartered in the City of Harrisburg. The public school system that exerts the greatest influence over the project is the Harrisburg School District. It has a yearly enrollment of approximately 11,500 students and operates 17 separate schools within the City. There are no schools within the project area; however, the Cameron Elementary School (grades K-4) at Muench and Green Streets is located immediately adjacent to the project area and obviously services the project area to some degree.
